<explanation>
Below is a tailored guide for drawing a detailed system‐design diagram of the MCP Registry project. The goal is to capture all the essential architectural elements—API server, service layer, persistence, external integrations, tooling, and deployment—so that any reader can understand how the pieces fit together and interact.

1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a backend-only, RESTful registry service written in Go.  
   - It exposes HTTP endpoints (health, ping, servers, publish) for managing metadata about MCP servers.  
   - It supports both MongoDB and in-memory stores, uses GitHub for authentication, and provides a CLI “publisher” tool to push entries.

2. Top‐Level Components to Represent  
   a. API Server Container (Go service)  
   b. Database (MongoDB or in-memory)  
   c. External Auth Service (GitHub OAuth)  
   d. CLI Publisher Tool  
   e. Utility Scripts (for testing)  
   f. Docker Compose/Container Orchestration

3. Core Internal Layers (within the API Server box)  
   - Configuration (internal/config)  
   - HTTP Server & Router (internal/api/server.go + internal/api/router)  
   - Handlers (internal/api/handlers/v0)  
   - Business Logic / Services (internal/service)  
   - Data Layer / Repositories (internal/database + internal/model)  
   - Auth Module (internal/auth)

4. Relationships & Data Flow  
   1) Client → HTTP(S) → API Server  
   2) Router dispatches to v0 handlers  
   3) Handlers call Service layer  
   4) Service layer uses Database interface (Mongo or Memory)  
   5) Service layer calls Auth module for “publish” endpoints (GitHub client)  
   6) Database persists/fetches data  
   7) CLI Publisher → HTTP POST /v0/publish → API Server  
   8) Docker Compose orchestrates API + MongoDB + seed import

5. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Hexagonal / Clean Architecture: clear separation between API adapters, business logic, persistence interfaces, and external clients.  
   - Dependency Injection via interfaces (database, auth).  
   - Layered approach: Router → Handlers → Services → Repositories.  
   - Pluggable data store (memory or Mongo) via strategy pattern.

6. Technologies & Frameworks  
   - Go modules, Go 1.18+  
   - Gin or built-in net/http (internal/api/router)  
   - MongoDB driver (internal/database/mongo)  
   - Docker & Docker Compose  
   - OpenAPI/Swagger (api/openapi.yaml, internal/docs)  
   - GitHub OAuth (internal/auth/github.go)  

7. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Draw each component as a box (use distinct shapes/colors):  
     • Container/VM: rounded box labeled “Docker Compose Network”  
     • API Service: large box subdivided into layers (Config, Router, Handlers, Service, Database)  
     • MongoDB: cylinder icon  
     • GitHub OAuth: external cloud symbol  
     • CLI Publisher: terminal icon  
     • Test Scripts: document icon  
   - Label arrows with protocols and call types (HTTP GET/POST, DB calls).  
   - Use directional arrows:  
     • Client → API Server (HTTP)  
     • API Server → MongoDB (TCP/Mongo protocol)  
     • Handlers → Service (in-process call)  
     • Service → Auth (HTTPS to GitHub API)  
     • CLI → API Server (HTTP POST)  
   - Color-code by layer type:  
     • Blue for API adapters  
     • Green for business logic  
     • Orange for persistence  
     • Gray for external services  

8. Step-by-Step Diagram Construction  
   a. Draw the “Docker Compose” boundary. Inside it, place two containers: “registry (Go API)” and “mongo (MongoDB)”.  
   b. Within the registry container, subdivide into:  
      - Config Module  
      - HTTP Server & Router  
      - Handlers (v0)  
      - Services (registry_service, fake_service)  
      - Database Abstraction (memory, mongo)  
      - Auth Module  
   c. Draw an arrow from HTTP Server → Handlers → Services → Database. Label each arrow (e.g., “Route to handler”, “Call registry_service”, “Query collection ‘servers_v2’”).  
   d. Draw an arrow from “Services” → “GitHub OAuth” cloud. Label “Validate bearer token / fetch app credentials”.  
   e. Outside the Docker boundary, place “Client” (web or CLI) and show HTTP calls (GET /v0/servers, POST /v0/publish).  
   f. Add “CLI Publisher” tool box, show an arrow to POST /v0/publish.  
   g. Add “scripts/test_endpoints.sh” box; arrow to /v0/health, /v0/servers.  
   h. Annotate seed data flow: arrow from “data/seed_2025_05_16.json” → “mongo” on first run (database/import.go).  

9. Final Tips  
   - Ensure every box is clearly labeled with package or directory path for clarity.  
   - Use a legend for color/shapes.  
   - Show directional arrows with annotations (method names or file paths).  
   - Highlight pluggable components (memory vs. mongo) by dashed outlines.  

By following this structure you’ll produce a diagram that:  
- Exposes all major code modules and how they interact  
- Clarifies external dependencies (MongoDB, GitHub)  
- Illustrates deployment topology (Docker Compose)  
- Demonstrates the CI/test tooling and CLI integrations  
- Uses color/shape conventions for rapid comprehension  
This level of detail ensures any engineer can quickly understand and extend the MCP Registry’s architecture.
